excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: It looks like `fcU` to said block should return `SYNCING` in this case if `newPayload` returned `ACCEPTED`. But yes, I would expect geth to execute a block if it has a parent block post-state which I think is the case when syncing to TTD is finished and if said block is the direct child of a terminal block

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content:
So, question, when this first fcU is received, it does
- Left PoW stage
- New skeleton head announced
- Synchronisation terminated
- Created initial skeleton subchain
- Starting reverse header sync cycle
- Fetching skeleton headers

what does this mean?

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: from my understanding, skeleton subchain is geth's backfill chain starting back from that fcU block

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: but geth wouldn't need to start a skeleton subchain in case its all synced upto TTD

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: yes -- wasn't the case here, but will know soon about that

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: (scenario i am assuming is : geth synced to TTD beforehand, first fcU referes to the terminal block as parent, and geth's terminal block is that parent , i.e.geth is not on a different fork)

excerpts.author: tersec
